classes.name: City of London aldermanic elections
classes.name_en: Aldermen of the City of London
classes.note: 25 aldermen, one per ward, elected by the ward's residents and business voters and standing again at least every six years, so ward polls fall in most years.

classes.note: Greater Manchester, Merseyside, South Yorkshire, Tyne and Wear, West Midlands, and West Yorkshire, elected in 1973, 1977, and 1981 and abolished with the Greater London Council on 1 April 1986 (Local Government Act 1985).

classes.name: Scottish regional, islands, and district council elections
classes.name_en: Scottish regions, islands areas, and districts, 1974 to 1994
classes.note: Nine regional councils, three islands councils, and 53 district councils, by first past the post: regions and islands in 1974, 1978, 1982, 1986, 1990, and 1994, districts in 1974, 1977, 1980, 1984, 1988, and 1992. Replaced by 32 unitary councils elected in April 1995.

classes.name: Council elections before the 1970s reorganizations
classes.name_en: Borough, county, burgh, and district councils before 1974
classes.note: Municipal boroughs from 1835 (annual elections by thirds each November), county councils from 1889 in England and Wales and 1890 in Scotland (triennial), urban and rural district and parish councils from 1894, burghs and Scottish county councils to 1975, and Northern Ireland's counties, boroughs, and districts to 1973. No national series was ever compiled; results survive in council minutes, local newspapers, and the municipal year books.
classes.disposition_reason: No official or compiled series exists before 1973: each council's results are in its own minutes and the local press, so the class waits until a national compilation is found.

classes.name: School board, education authority, and poor law guardian elections
classes.name_en: School boards, Scottish education authorities, boards of guardians, and Scottish parish councils
classes.note: School boards in England and Wales (1870 to 1903, cumulative vote) and Scotland (1873 to 1919); Scottish education authorities (1919 to 1928, single transferable vote); boards of guardians of the poor (1834 to 1930) and Scotland's parish councils (1895 to 1930). All were abolished by the Education Act 1902 and the Local Government Acts of 1929.
classes.disposition_reason: Results survive only in board minutes and local newspapers; no official compilation exists.

classes.name: Parish, town, and Welsh community council elections
classes.note: About 10,000 parish and town councils in England and 735 community and town councils in Wales, usually elected with the principal council; most seats are filled without a poll. No national results file exists: notices of uncontested elections and declarations of results sit on each principal council's site. Northern Ireland has no parish tier.
classes.name_en: Parish and town councils in England, community and town councils in Wales

cadence.administered_by: The principal council's returning officer
cadence.vacancy_rule: By-election if ten electors ask within 14 days of notice, otherwise co-option.

cadence.administered_by: The principal council's returning officer

classes.name: Scottish community council elections
classes.note: About 1,200 active community councils, each formed under its council's scheme of establishment, with cycles of three or four years that differ by council; nearly all form without a ballot. Councils publish notices of uncontested elections and, rarely, declarations of results.

cadence.administered_by: Each council under its scheme for community councils

classes.name: National park authority elections (Scotland)
classes.name_en: Elected members of the Cairngorms and Loch Lomond and The Trossachs national park authorities
classes.note: Five members of each authority are elected by the park's residents in five wards, by first past the post; the Cairngorms poll is run by the Highland Council (next on 25 March 2027), Loch Lomond and The Trossachs by Stirling Council as a postal ballot. The other English and Welsh national park authorities are appointed.

cadence.administered_by: The Highland Council (Cairngorms)
Stirling Council (Loch Lomond and The Trossachs)

classes.name: Health board elections (Scotland)
classes.name_en: Directly elected members of NHS Dumfries and Galloway and NHS Fife
classes.note: A pilot under the Health Boards (Membership and Elections) (Scotland) Act 2009: one board-wide election in each of the two boards on 10 June 2010, by single transferable vote with postal and online voting, for four-year terms. The pilots were not extended.

classes.name: Council governance and mayoral referendums
classes.name_en: Referendums on a directly elected mayor or a council's governance
classes.note: Held on a petition of 5 percent of electors, a council resolution, or a government direction, under the Local Government Act 2000 and the Localism Act 2011; the 2012 round in ten cities was ordered by the government.

cadence.administered_by: The council's counting officer

classes.name: Council tax referendums
classes.note: Required when a billing or precepting authority sets an increase above the principles the government sets each year. Only one has been held: the Bedfordshire police and crime commissioner's precept on 7 May 2015, which was rejected.

dates.note: Bedfordshire police and crime commissioner's precept.

classes.name: Neighbourhood planning referendums
classes.note: A neighborhood development plan, order, or community right to build order takes effect only after a referendum in its area, with a second business referendum where the area is mainly commercial. About 1,800 plans were in force by March 2025; no central register of results exists, so each planning authority's pages are the source.

cadence.administered_by: The local planning authority's counting officer

classes.name: Parish and community polls
classes.name_en: Parish polls in England and community polls in Wales
classes.note: A poll demanded at a parish meeting (Local Government Act 1972, Schedule 12, paragraph 18) or a community meeting in Wales, run by the district council; advisory, held on any question, dozens a year. Notices of poll and results are on the principal councils' sites only.

classes.name: Council-run advisory polls
classes.name_en: Advisory polls run by councils and authorities
classes.note: Non-binding polls a council or authority chose to hold, such as Strathclyde's water poll (1994), Milton Keynes's council tax poll (1999), Edinburgh's congestion charge (2005), and Greater Manchester's congestion charge (2008).

classes.name: Welsh Sunday opening polls
classes.name_en: Local polls on Sunday opening of public houses in Wales
classes.note: Every seven years from 1961 to 1996, each Welsh county or district voted on whether its public houses could open on Sundays; by 1996 only Dwyfor stayed dry. The polls ended when the Licensing Act 2003 repealed sections 66 and 67 of the Licensing Act 1964.

classes.name: Recall petitions
classes.note: Opened by the Speaker after a custodial sentence, a suspension of ten sitting days or more, or an expenses conviction; the MP loses the seat if 10 percent of the constituency's electors sign within six weeks. The petition officer publishes the number of signatures. Six petitions were held from 2018 to 2023 (North Antrim, Brecon and Radnorshire, Peterborough, Rutherglen and Hamilton West, Wellingborough, and one ended by resignation).

cadence.administered_by: The petition officer (the constituency's acting returning officer)

classes.name: Party leadership and candidate selection ballots
classes.name_en: Party leadership and candidate selection ballots
classes.note: Includes the open primaries some parties tried for parliamentary candidates in 2009 and 2010, which the parties ran and paid for.
classes.disposition_reason: Parties run their own leadership elections and candidate selections; no authority administers or certifies them, and the UK has no state-run primaries.

classes.name: Crofting Commission elections
classes.note: Six of the nine commissioners are elected by crofters in six areas every five years (2012, 2017, 2022).
classes.disposition_reason: Only crofters vote, so the electorate is a sectoral roll, not the register of electors (scope decision of 2026-11-11).

classes.name: Business improvement district and other sectoral ballots
classes.name_en: Business improvement district and other sectoral ballots
classes.note: About 70 business improvement district ballots a year; results are on the councils' sites if they are ever wanted.
classes.disposition_reason: Business improvement district ballots (non-domestic ratepayers voting on a levy), Common Hall (liverymen electing the Lord Mayor and sheriffs), housing transfer and tenant ballots, school parent ballots, NHS foundation trust governors, and youth parliaments are not polls of the register of electors (scope decision of 2026-11-11).
